# Forge

> Strongly typed state transition planning for .NET 10.

Forge is an MIT-licensed .NET library family by Pjotr Casteel.

Canonical website: https://pjotrcasteel.github.io/Forge/
Canonical repository: https://github.com/pjotrcasteel/Forge

## Packages

- Forge.Delta — source-generated semantic object differences.
  - NuGet: https://www.nuget.org/packages/Forge.Delta
- Forge.Sync — source-generated desired-state reconciliation and typed planning. Depends on Forge.Delta.
  - NuGet: https://www.nuget.org/packages/Forge.Sync

Current family version: 1.20.0

## Core boundary

Forge calculates, classifies, validates, explains and simulates transitions.
Forge does not persist state, call external systems, publish messages, authorize actions or execute plans.

## Start here

- README: https://github.com/pjotrcasteel/Forge
- API contract: https://github.com/pjotrcasteel/Forge/blob/main/docs/API_CONTRACT.md
- Design: https://github.com/pjotrcasteel/Forge/blob/main/docs/DESIGN.md
- Reconciliation: https://github.com/pjotrcasteel/Forge/blob/main/docs/RECONCILIATION.md

## Important semantics

- Delta answers: what changed inside one object?
- Sync answers: how do keyed current and desired collections differ?
- Replace means complete desired state; current-only items may be removed.
- Upsert means partial desired input; current-only items are preserved.
- Generated normal hot paths use direct property access rather than runtime reflection.
- Logical keys, execution states, facts, reasons, approval scopes and invariant violations remain consumer CLR types.
- Portable manifests are data, not executable code.
